newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks soar on cricket euphoria, rains.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks soar on cricket euphoria, rains.

text.p: The Zimbabwe Stock Exchange hit a new peak on Friday, buoyed by continuing rains, lower money market rates and local euphoria as the southern African state looked set to make cricket history against England.
The key 57-share industrial index leapt 83.05 points to break through the 8,900 psychological barrier, ending the day at a new record high of 8,922.65. It surged 174.65 ponts on the week.
"I think the good rains and the euphoria over the way Zimbabwe has played (cricket) against England has pushed the market higher," one broker said.
On Friday, Zimbabwe beat England by 131 runs in the third and final one day international series in Harare. It won the series 3-0, its first ever over any side.
"That (the cricket victory) has put everyone in a good mood and has also helped to boost confidence overall. Confidence is what drives the market," another broker said.
"The continuing lower rates on the money market are also driving people to the stock market and I think its going to continue strong into next week before selling pressure sets in," he added.

Among the bourse's winners on Friday, clothing retailer Edgars soared 500 cents to 4,200, publishing group Zimpapers jumped 150 cents to 2,350, clothing Truworths rose 75 cents to 1,075 while horticultural group Ariston and bankers Barclays climbed 50 cents each to 2,500 and 2,550 respectively.

Electronics group Apex gained 20 cents to 220 while construction and plastics investor IHL, seed manufacturer and distributor SeedCo and hotel chain Zimsun put on 10 cents each to 1,870, 240 and 415 respectively.

Against the trend, finance group Finhold slid 150 cents to 700 following announcement of year-end results showing no dividend and lower share earnings, construction firm Mash shed 15 cents to 275 and steel window company Radar lost 10 cents to 360.
Minings were lacklustre with Wankie Colliery trading 10 cents up at 620 while copper miner Mhangura added five cents to 25.
The seven-counter mining index put on 4.83 points to close at 1,117.75, a rise of 51.41 points on the week.
